question: Explain whether merchandise sales changed mainly because of order volume or average merchandise per order. If sales declined, drill down by category and seller.

evidence.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-05-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-06-01') THEN o.order_id END) AS baseline_orders, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-05-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-06-01') THEN COALESCE(i.price,0) ELSE 0 END),2) AS baseline_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-06-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-07-01') THEN o.order_id END) AS target_orders, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-06-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-07-01') THEN COALESCE(i.price,0) ELSE 0 END),2) AS target_sales FROM orders o LEFT JOIN order_items i ON o.order_id=i.order_id WHERE (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-05-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-06-01') OR (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-06-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-07-01')

SELECT p.product_category_name AS dimension_key, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-06-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-07-01') THEN o.order_id END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-05-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-06-01') THEN o.order_id END) AS change_value FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON i.order_id=o.order_id LEFT JOIN products p ON i.product_id=p.product_id WHERE ((o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-05-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-06-01') OR (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-06-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-07-01')) GROUP BY p.product_category_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-06-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-07-01') THEN o.order_id END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-05-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-06-01') THEN o.order_id END) < 0 ORDER BY change_value, p.product_category_name NULLS LAST LIMIT 5

SELECT i.seller_id AS dimension_key, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-06-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-07-01') THEN o.order_id END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-05-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-06-01') THEN o.order_id END) AS change_value FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON i.order_id=o.order_id LEFT JOIN products p ON i.product_id=p.product_id WHERE ((o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-05-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-06-01') OR (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-06-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-07-01')) AND p.product_category_name = 'relogios_presentes' GROUP BY i.seller_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-06-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-07-01') THEN o.order_id END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-05-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-06-01') THEN o.order_id END) < 0 ORDER BY change_value, i.seller_id NULLS LAST LIMIT 5

decisions.reason: Need to compare order count and average merchandise per order between 2018-06 and 2018-05 to determine whether sales changed due to volume or per-order amount.

Merchandise sales declined from 996,517.68 to 865,124.31 while orders dropped from 6,873 to 6,167, so the decline is associated with lower order volume; the next step is to rank categories by decline in distinct orders to drill down per the question.

Sales declined (996,517.68 → 865,124.31) with orders also down, and the leading declining category is relogios_presentes. To drill down by seller within that category as requested, rank seller order-count declines.
